title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The ‘Improving Socio-Economic Status for Women, Youth and Marginalized Groups’ project in Mongu, Kaoma Namwala, Gwembe districts in Zambia, implemented by Oxfam through ICSP will reach 15,600 people directly from vulnerable households including female, child and elderly headed households. Oxfam will partner with Young Women Christian Association (YWCA), Nutri Aid Trust and Women for Change (WfC) to deliver activities promoting local humanitarian leadership, anticipatory action systems and forecast based financing, agriculture and food systems, transformative women’s leadership, economic empowerment and ending violence against women and girls.. OUTCOME: IMPACT 1: People experiencing poverty and most vulnerable to shocks, conflicts and crises have more sustainable and equitable access to food and livelihoods. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: This programme outcome focuses on building capacity of smallholder farmers on climate smart agriculture, soil and natural resource conservation, organic manure making and application, cultivation of drought tolerant crops, irrigation, mechanisation, postharvest management to reduce harvest losses and use of renewable energy in food production and value chains. This is a critical intervention under this impact area of the programme and would have not been funded if this intervention was not implemented.
